problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}6x+5y-3z=2 \\ 4x-5y+kz=1 \\ -2x+10y-5z=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that  $x=\frac{1}{2}$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $160-70k,$ find the value of $k.$
worked_solution:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}6 & 5 & -2 \\ 4 & -5 & k \\ -2 & 10 & -5\end{aligned}|=160-70k\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $x$ is given by $x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{x}=|\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & -3 \\ 1 & -5 & k \\ -2 & 10 & -5\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-5 & k \\ 10 & -5\end{aligned}|-5\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & k \\ -2 & -5\end{aligned}|+(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & -5 \\ -2 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(25-10k)-5(-5+2k)-3(10-10) \\  & =50-20k+25-10k+0 \\  & =75-30k.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
x=\frac{{D}_{x}}{D}=\frac{75-30k}{160-70k}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $x=\frac{1}{2}.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{75-30k}{160-70k} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ 2(75-30k) & =160-70k \\ 150-60k & =160-70k \\ 10k & =10 \\ k & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
